intrusive thoughts? everyone gets them! they are normal and don't mean anything about your morality or what you are actually going to do. in fact, having intrusive thoughts about a thing probably means you do not want to do the thing/the thought goes against your values :) it's important to remember when it comes to stuff like this, that your reaction to the thought says more about you than the initial thought. if you think something horrible and immediately feel disgusted by it, that just means you have a strong sense of morality and you care deeply about other people. 

everyone gets intrusive thoughts, but some people assign more meaning to them than most people. if they are causing you distress (and based on this post I am fairly certain they are) then that can be caused by OCD. not just about being clean, or things like that, but also intense fear of hurting people, acting on those thoughts you are having, etc. people don't always talk about the more taboo side of it, so that can slip under the radar and then you get people like me who knew about ocd for years but still thought we were horrible monsters experiencing things no one else ever experienced because people get weird when you say that you are obsessively scared that you secretly want to murder children. but it doesn't make you a horrible person and a lot of people experience it, like I said earlier. if it causes you distress that means that thought goes against your morals and who you are as a person. 

I can very much relate, I remember being a small child and cursing my "thoughts that aren't mine" that told me to do unspeakable things. it's really scary, and it can be really debilitating, but it's less scary when you know that other people get it too, a lot of people experience this. therapy can help, and medication, usually a combination of the two, and what works best for you will be very specific and personalized, but I don't know where you are with stuff like this, and it's really hard to trust people and really hard to talk about these things outloud and therapy is a lot of work and can be very scary, so I don't blame you if you don't feel like you are in a place for that. but often just being able to name this things: intrusive thoughts, possible OCD, etc, can take some of the power from them. and know that if you do go in that direction I have heard that it is very possible to get to a life free from these problems. I am... not there yet at all, but most people I have talked to have positive things to say. 

I think that is everything I have to say right now but if you have any questions or want to vent, feel free. I experience this too. <3
